The repo's transcription of the 2026.9.18 manual includes an E-7 change-of-status case for registered D-1, D-2, D-4~D-10 and E-1~E-6 holders (E-6-2 excluded), so all of E-1~E-5 are covered, and E-7-1 has a `change` list. I could not re-fetch the manual online (search budget used up, WebFetch DNS failure), so this rests on the repo's 2026 manual transcription plus an earlier verifier's quote.

verdicts.reason: The claim holds. F-3's `next` is E-7-1, E-2, D-2-2/3/4, D-10-1, F-2-99, F-2-71, F-6-1, F-5-13 and F-2-3, with no E-1, E-3, E-4 or E-5. The repo's 2026 manual transcription has a change case for the F-3 spouse of an E-1~E-5/E-6 (not E-6-2)/E-7 professional in the E-1, E-3, E-4 and E-5 lists, and in the E-6 list too. The fix needs two changes. First, E-1 and E-3 are also open to F-3 holders through general cases (high-level talent on a non-work visa; researchers at special-law or national institutes from any status), so bare edges are right for them. E-4 and E-5, however, are open in Korea only to D-2/D-10 holders and to the spouse of an E-x professional. The engine cannot know the spouse's status, so those moves need a note, and a move note replaces the visa's 'how', so the note must restate it. Second, E-6-1 has the same spouse case and should be added the same way. Simulation (spouse=foreigner, edu 3) shows E-1, E-4, E-5 and E-6-1 OPEN and E-3 correctly BLOCKED by edu.

verdicts.reason: True: F-3 has one in-edge (NONE), while visadocs has an F-3 `change` list. The fix's handling of short-term statuses is wrong. The 2026 manual's general in-Korea change to F-3, as transcribed, applies only after entry and on humanitarian grounds (pregnancy, birth, child-raising, illness) for visa-free or short-term entrants, and requires a statement of reasons. The map already treats every short-term → family move (F-6-1, F-2-3) as `abroad: true`, and the review marked that correct. `abroadFor: notified` would show an ordinary in-Korea change to every non-notified tourist; it rests only on the 2022 Visa Navigator's D-2-family line, which I could not check against 2026 text. For lawful long-term residents (D-2, D-4, F-1), plain in-Korea edges are right, and F-3's own needs gate them. Simulation: D-2-2 → F-3 is OPEN for spouse=foreigner and BLOCKED for spouse=none.

verdicts.reason: True that F-6-1 has no F-1 move, and the route exists in 2026. The manual has '혼인단절 결혼이민자 가사정리를 위한 방문동거 체류기간 연장허가' in both the F-1 and F-6 chapters. Three corrections. (1) The 2026 manual labels the sub-code F-1-6 (가사정리), not F-1-11. (2) The manual handles it as an extension of stay, and F-1 has only an `extend` list in visadocs. visadocs.js makeMove reads `within` rules only for same-status moves, so F-6-1 → F-1 would show no document list unless that is handled. (3) The edge should be gated like F-6-3 with spouse: exKorean, so a still-married reader is not offered it. Simulation: OPEN for spouse=exKorean, BLOCKED for spouse=korean.

verdicts.reason: True that no visa lists G-1-5, and 난민법 제5조 lets any foreigner in Korea file a refugee claim. The proposed edges are wrong. G-1-5 has only an `extend` list in the 2026 manual (34. 기타(G-1)), so in-Korea edges would break the edge/document invariant. G-1-5 has no gate, so every tourist, student and E-9 worker would see 'Refugee applicant' as an OPEN planning option (confirmed by simulation from B-2). A refugee claim is not a migration route a planning map should recommend. The seven source statuses chosen are arbitrary. The path is not dead either: G-1-5 is in the current-visa search list, so a reader who already holds it can start there and reach F-2-4 → F-5-27. This matches round-2 visit#7, which made the same call.
verdicts.correctedFix:
Add no edges. Keep G-1-5 (and G-1-6) as start-only nodes and record the decision with a comment above G-1-5 in data/visamap.yaml:
  # G-1-5 and G-1-6 are start-only on purpose: a refugee claim is not a route the map
  # recommends, and the 2026 manual documents only an extension list for them. Readers who
  # already hold one pick it as their current visa.
